_comment: World bible section 13. Seven Reaches on the small map, one for each Sea (the Far Sea's ice and its whaling chain are one Reach, Rime), so a Sea and its archipelago are the same thing at this size. Sugar, Whalers' and Mirage are held back for the larger maps alongside Scrap — each shared a Sea with a Reach that survives, and each sat on a painted cluster too crowded or too sparse to chart clearly. Island counts are set by how many clearly separated islands each painted cluster holds. Each Reach has a role in the opening (docs/opening.md): home is the Crown's, contested Reaches open with two islands a side, open Reaches are charted and nobody's, frontier Reaches start unexplored and hide the Confederacy's base. An island marked port is one of the three port cities on the Aldermain, Sovereign Reach's great island. Each island carries a `seed`: the number the world's look, its creature and its garrison mix are drawn from. It used to be computed from the island's name, which meant renaming an island silently re-rolled its terrain, its deposits and what lives in its water. It is written down here instead, frozen at the value it had on 19 September, so the Star Wars rename changed names and nothing else.

islands.name: Avermere
islands.note: Crown grain and cattle. The fleet eats from here.

islands.name: Ballmoor
islands.note: Foundries. The Crown's arms come from here.

islands.name: Bracton
islands.note: Ropewalks and sailcloth. Unglamorous and indispensable.

islands.name: Chandler's Rest
islands.note: Hale's birthplace; quietly Confederacy-leaning.

islands.name: Corsham Head
islands.note: The signal station that watches the approach to the Aldermain.

islands.name: Highwater
islands.note: The Crown's walled capital, behind seawalls three hundred feet high. It stands on the Aldermain, the one great island, far larger than anything else, with the best ground and the best resources in the world.

islands.name: Gorley
islands.note: Site of an old massacre. Hates the Crown.

islands.name: Sievern
islands.note: Quarry island. Every seawall in the Crown Sea started here.

islands.name: Ulverne
islands.note: Assize island: the Crown's courts, and the gallows behind them.

islands.name: Yarrow Minor
islands.note: The royal dockyard.

islands.name: Kingsward
islands.note: The Imperium's naval academy.

islands.name: Minterne
islands.note: Banking houses. Half the war is paid for here.

islands.name: Cartmel
islands.note: The Great Library: charts and archives.

islands.name: Chepstow
islands.note: Market island. Prices set here are quoted three Seas away.

islands.name: Marlbury
islands.note: Garrison town. Regiments are raised and drilled here.

islands.name: Wrightsport
islands.note: Shipwright capital of the Seven Seas; Reyne's home port.

islands.name: Starcross
islands.note: Old seafaring people. The best navigators the Crown can hire.

islands.name: Starpath
islands.note: Where navigators are taught. A course is remembered as a chant, not a chart.

islands.name: Shellhouse
islands.note: Shell wind-chimes hang in every doorway; the Shoal-folk read the air by them.

islands.name: Outrigger Bay
islands.note: Where the canoes are built. Lashed timber, no nails, no keels.

islands.name: Longreef
islands.note: Forty miles of reef with one channel through it, and only locals know it.

islands.name: Palmfall
islands.note: Copra, coir and drinking nuts. The Crown calls it unimproved.

islands.name: Driftway
islands.note: Everything lost in the Long Sea washes up here eventually, including people.

islands.name: Nine Reefs
islands.note: Nine atolls, one lagoon, and the best sheltered anchorage in the Reach.

islands.name: Gibbet Rock
islands.note: An Imperium prison. The name is not a metaphor.

islands.name: Gardenholm
islands.note: Sacred and green. No tree on it has ever been cut.

islands.name: The Kettles
islands.note: Prison mines, cutting ambergris out of a dead leviathan's skull.

islands.name: Anchorite Rock
islands.note: Hermit island.

islands.name: Ravenscar
islands.note: Wreckers’ coast. Lights are shown here on bad nights, and not to help.

islands.name: Wrackham
islands.note: Built entirely from salvage, including the church.

islands.name: Slaughden
islands.note: Half under water. The streets are rowed, not walked.

islands.name: Coffinswell
islands.note: The Hushed keep to what's left of it. They are not heard arriving.

islands.name: Belfry Shoal
islands.note: Open water with one bell tower standing out of it. The bell still rings on the swell.

islands.name: Northreach
islands.note: Torvik's homeland. Urskin whalers and harpooners.

islands.name: Tallow Cay
islands.note: Whale-oil and salt. Far enough out that nobody counts the ships.

islands.name: Sharpness
islands.note: A cutter base, of sorts.

islands.name: Rime Island
islands.note: Frozen rock. Nothing here but weather.

islands.name: Frostwick
islands.note: Ice-locked five months a year; the Crown's charts stop being useful here.

islands.name: Varrow
islands.note: Fairweather's floating market: a city of lashed-together hulks.

islands.name: Keelhaven
islands.note: Where Urskin clans winter their great keels and repair them in the dark.

islands.name: Greenholm
islands.note: Forested and heavily patrolled. Something large is being finished here.

islands.name: Firewatch
islands.note: An active volcano. The ash never quite settles.

islands.name: Leeward Keep
islands.note: Admiral Blackwater's private fortress. The water below it is always flat.

islands.name: Tundvik
islands.note: The edge of the charts.

islands.name: Reedmoot
islands.note: Where the Bog-folk clans meet. Crown officers are received, never invited.

islands.name: Sorrowhead
islands.note: A drowned village nobody rebuilt, and nobody will say why.

islands.name: Brimstone Cay
islands.note: Sulphur. It gets into the powder, the food and the lungs.

islands.name: Basilisk Rock
islands.note: Sheer, snake-ridden, and the only deep anchorage for sixty miles.

islands.name: Cane Hollow
islands.note: Sugar cane, fever, and the conjure-women the clans left behind.

islands.name: Powder Isle
islands.note: Saltpetre. Every gun in the Seven Seas owes this rock.

islands.name: Saltgrave
islands.note: A salt-slave island. One side never sees dusk.

islands.name: Blackreef
islands.note: Jubal the Fat's corsair haven. Debts are collected here.

islands.name: The Terraces
islands.note: Rice breadbasket of the Outer Seas.

islands.name: The White Flats
islands.note: Salt to the horizon. Ships are visible from a day away, which suits nobody.

islands.name: Chaswell
islands.note: The last watering stop before the flats. Water costs what the seller says.

islands.name: Scaldwell
islands.note: Hot springs and boiling pools; the water is undrinkable and the fish are not.

islands.name: Noonday Rock
islands.note: No shade anywhere on it. A punishment posting.

islands.name: Salthouse
islands.note: Curing houses. Half the fleet's salt beef comes through here.

islands.name: Coralhome
islands.note: Crown-held. The Reef-folk sang their ships into shape here for generations; the Crown cleared the reef to build a proper harbor.

islands.name: Hearsay Cay
islands.note: Home of the Rumor Guild, who sell to both sides.

islands.name: Graving Bay
islands.note: The great civilian dockyards.

islands.name: Newmarket
islands.note: Gambling and racing. Everyone owes someone here.

islands.name: Preston's Reach
islands.note: Signal towers. Word travels fast from here.

islands.name: The Shoals
islands.note: The Shoal-folk: webbed, night-eyed, and the best watchers in the world.

islands.name: Hawksbill Bay
islands.note: Amber and turtle-shell. Three harbors and no customs house.

islands.name: Denby Cay
islands.note: Sugar and rum. Old money, and none of it decided.

islands.name: Singing Shallows
islands.note: A nursery reef. Hulls are grown here, and the singing does not stop at night.
